text:
Bitcoin trades near $61,800 as the market enters a structural consolidation phase, with over 50% of BTC supply now underwater — a stress signal last observed in Q4 2022. The Federal Reserve, now under Chair Kevin Warsh, held rates at 3.5–3.75% but is signaling a departure from its easing bias following May's 172,000 jobs print and a CPI reading of 3.8–4.2%. Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows across multiple May sessions, while corporate treasury accumulation — a key 2025 price driver — has materially thinned.

Globally, Japan's parliament passed landmark legislation on June 11 classifying crypto as a financial instrument, cutting capital gains tax to 20% by 2028 and opening the door to domestic crypto ETFs. The EU's MiCA framework moved into active enforcement, and U.S. options position limit filings for BTC ETFs signal growing derivatives maturity.

The DXY holds near 99–100, supported by sticky inflation and Middle East safe-haven flows, while the S&P 500 consolidates near 7,200 amid major bank warnings on overcrowded positioning. When dollar strength persists alongside elevated yields, Bitcoin historically underperforms equities — the current setup echoes Q3 2022 transmission patterns, suggesting digital assets remain tethered to macro risk appetite until the FOMC June 16–17 meeting delivers clarity.
